purpose: Tie automatic resource production into the civilizations, settlements, architecture and trade network so farms feel like believable parts of the world rather than machines placed inside themed shells.
resource_design_doctrine: Every major farm is treated as a local industry with workers, storage, maintenance, transport, civic context and a reason for being located where it is.
The visible architecture belongs to the civilization; the redstone/mechanical core may be standardized internally where useful.
Primary processing stays near the resource ecosystem that feeds it. The Grand Exchange sorts, stores, prices and redistributes goods but does not become the universal processing island.
Imports and exports should be physically legible through docks, railheads, canals, roads, warehouses, barges, carts, portals or freight halls.
A production island must contain ordinary life and non-production space so it reads as a settlement with an economy rather than a farm perimeter.
Dangerous farms justify separation, walls, depth, height, containment yards or remote compounds. Safe farms should be integrated much more closely with homes and public space.
Byproducts matter. Bone meal, compost, fuel, drops, storage overflow and processing waste should create secondary structures and trade relationships instead of disappearing abstractly.

Resource abundance should influence local architecture. Timber-rich regions use timber generously; stone-rich regions build mass; ceramic regions surface buildings with tile/brick; imported materials should look more prestigious or strategically placed.
Resource scarcity is as important as abundance. A civilization that imports most timber should not casually build enormous wooden districts unless the architecture explains that wealth or dependence.
Trade routes are gameplay infrastructure and worldbuilding simultaneously. Repeated resource flows should eventually be represented by named routes and visible transfer nodes.

Agriculture.why_here: Flat fertile land, canal culture and existing water councils make large-scale agriculture a natural foundation of Breadbasket civilization rather than a farm imposed after the fact.
Agriculture.farm_architecture: Field grids, irrigation channels, long barns, granaries, wind/water mills, compost yards, moss/bone-meal support compounds and canal-side loading sheds.
Agriculture.settlement_expression: Villages sit at field/canal intersections. The capital is a produce market and administrative water town; bulk production lives on rural estates; milling and shipping concentrate at the canal port.
local_processing: basic food preparation that directly follows farm output
Agriculture.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Compost and moss loops become visible fertilizer yards; excess plant material feeds animal and brewing ecosystems; storage overflow creates seasonal granary annexes rather than invisible buffers.
Agriculture.player_build_guidance: Do not hide the farm behind a decorative village. Make irrigation, storage and field logistics the village's reason for existing.

Wood & Tree.why_here: Forest guild law, river transport and a culture built around stewardship make the full tree collection believable as one regional industry.
Wood & Tree.farm_architecture: Managed groves, monumental timber frames concealing automated tree systems, sawmills, log ponds, drying yards, propagation nurseries, seed/sapling libraries and log-export docks.
Wood & Tree.settlement_expression: Raw growth, milling, finished carpentry, specialty groves, stewardship/knowledge and export are separated into different settlements while remaining one regional economy.
local_processing: charcoal or wood-derived processing where appropriate
exports: specialty/Nether wood under the intentional consolidation rule
trade_routes: timber freight to Hearthlands and shipbuilding regions
Wood & Tree.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Saplings and propagation feed the arboretum; excess plant material can support compost/fuel; stripped/log variants become separate warehouse classes rather than clutter.
Wood & Tree.player_build_guidance: The automated tree farm should read as a managed forestry structure or grove district, not a redstone box surrounded by fake trees.

Food & Brewing.why_here: Hearthlands culture already centers hospitality, inns, cellars and local food. It is the natural place for turning imported and local ingredients into prepared goods.
Food & Brewing.farm_architecture: Breweries, malt houses, smokehouses, bakeries, cellars, kitchens, orchard presses, communal ovens and inn storehouses embedded in ordinary neighborhoods.
Food & Brewing.settlement_expression: Production is deliberately domestic and social. The brewery town can be work-heavy, but the regional capital should feel like a place where the outputs are consumed and celebrated.
local_processing: food autocrafting where it directly belongs to the recipe chain
imports: Isles of Plenty tropical ingredients and honey
trade_routes: traveler supply contracts with Transit Isles
Food & Brewing.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Spent ingredients and organic waste should return to compost/agriculture loops when useful; bottles/containers create demand for Artisan Coast glasswork.
Food & Brewing.player_build_guidance: Let the farm chain disappear into believable kitchens, cellars and breweries. Players should understand what a building makes without seeing every mechanism.

Passive Animal & Creature.why_here: Year-round lush terrain, open architecture and a stewardship-oriented culture let animal systems feel like husbandry landscapes instead of compact mob machinery.
Passive Animal & Creature.farm_architecture: Pasture compounds, shaded barns, breeding courtyards, collection sheds, sanctuary edges, feed stores and open market pavilions.
Passive Animal & Creature.settlement_expression: Animal production is broken into landscaped neighborhoods and compounds with large green buffers; the preserved interior keeps the civilization from reading as one huge ranch.
local_processing: collection and sorting of animal outputs
basic food processing where directly tied to husbandry
imports: Stone Highlands/Artisan Coast durable flooring and decorative materials
exports: creature-specific drops supported by passive systems
trade_routes: Southern sea road to Sapphire Coast
Passive Animal & Creature.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Manure is abstracted through compost/fertilizer exchange rather than literal new mechanics; wool and leather move to craft markets; food output feeds Hearthlands.
Passive Animal & Creature.player_build_guidance: Prioritize visible habitat, shade and husbandry space. Hide collection systems beneath/behind believable barns and handling yards.

Village, Iron & Raid.why_here: The most centralized civic state naturally owns the archipelago's strongest villager administration, defensive institutions and iron-linked production.
Village, Iron & Raid.farm_architecture: Civic housing blocks, guild/work halls, ironworks courtyards, fortified raid-training/containment district, barracks, armories and administrative buildings.
Village, Iron & Raid.settlement_expression: Villager systems should look like real neighborhoods and institutions. Iron production belongs to civic/industrial courtyards; raid systems belong to the military edge rather than the public square.
Village, Iron & Raid.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Iron supports nearly every region's tools/infrastructure; raid drops supply niche systems; villager trade outputs should feed Grand Exchange rather than being warehoused only locally.
Village, Iron & Raid.player_build_guidance: Do not expose villagers as farm components. Build neighborhoods, dormitories, guilds and civic service structures around the mechanics.

Storage, Sorting & Logistics.why_here: The Grand Exchange exists because goods from every specialized region meet here. Its function is movement, buffering and market organization, not replacing source-region processing.
Storage, Sorting & Logistics.farm_architecture: Warehouse blocks, sorter halls, bonded stores, auction courts, freight yards, cranes, customs basins and guild offices.
Storage, Sorting & Logistics.settlement_expression: Different islands separate the social market city, bulk freight/storage, customs/import handling and guild/finance functions.
local_processing: packaging/autocrafting only when it is genuinely logistics rather than source processing
Storage, Sorting & Logistics.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Overflow becomes auction lots, reserve warehouses or return freight. Storage expansion should create visible new warehouse phases instead of one endlessly enlarged basement.
Storage, Sorting & Logistics.player_build_guidance: Keep the Exchange visibly dependent on other regions. If a resource can be processed meaningfully at its source, do not move that processing here.

Redstone Engineering.why_here: A technical guild city-state is the natural home for component fabrication, test rigs, autocrafting development and standardized machine systems used elsewhere.
Redstone Engineering.farm_architecture: Machine halls, test yards, component shops, utility corridors, rail works, prototype towers and demonstration viaducts.
Redstone Engineering.settlement_expression: One island operates as several technical districts separated by residences, guild halls and civic demonstration spaces.
imports: Nether quartz and specialty materials via Ember Coast
Redstone Engineering.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Prototype/obsolete machinery becomes visible yard clutter or museum pieces; standardized components support farms across every region.
Redstone Engineering.player_build_guidance: Use a shared internal machine language, but wrap each exported system in the destination civilization's architecture instead of cloning Engineer's Reach buildings everywhere.

Glass, Concrete & Colorworks.why_here: A coastal craft republic already values workshops, color, glazing and visible artisanal production; imported raw materials become high-value finished surfaces here.
Glass, Concrete & Colorworks.farm_architecture: Glass furnaces, dye courts, concrete yards, tile shops, pigment storage, gallery markets and sample arcades.
Glass, Concrete & Colorworks.settlement_expression: Separate craft quarters share one inhabited coastal city; production fronts onto streets and courtyards rather than hiding behind a factory wall.
imports: sand/gravel and specialty inputs from source regions
Glass, Concrete & Colorworks.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Samples and imperfect batches can populate workshop yards and markets; finished materials visibly reappear in elite buildings across other civilizations.
Glass, Concrete & Colorworks.player_build_guidance: This region should be where imported raw color becomes architecture. Use its output to explain why later/wealthier districts elsewhere gain colored glass, tile or concrete accents.

Stone & Geology.why_here: Quarry cliffs and a mason-guild civilization make bulk stone, generation systems and finished masonry believable as one regional chain.
Stone & Geology.farm_architecture: Open quarries, generator halls disguised as water/stone works, cutting yards, block cranes, bridge test yards and inclined freight roads.
Stone & Geology.settlement_expression: Raw extraction, renewable stone generation, finished masonry craft and export freight are distinct settlements with the same massive architectural language.
Stone & Geology.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Excess cobble feeds infrastructure and fill; high-quality cut stone becomes a prestige export to Crownlands and High Kingdom.
Stone & Geology.player_build_guidance: Make renewable stone production look like a deliberate water/geology works rather than pretending everything came from a quarry.

Mud, Clay & Ceramics.why_here: Clay-rich terrain, water scarcity and a civilization organized around cisterns/kilns make the full ceramic chain culturally central.
Mud, Clay & Ceramics.farm_architecture: Clay settling ponds, mud fields, brickworks, long kilns, glaze yards, pottery courtyards, cisterns and aqueducts.
Mud, Clay & Ceramics.settlement_expression: Raw gathering, bulk brick, colored terracotta, fine pottery and water infrastructure occupy different towns while sharing courtyard and shade logic.
Mud, Clay & Ceramics.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Ceramic outputs should visibly appear in Engineer's Reach roofs/floors, Artisan Coast decorative work and Hearthlands kitchens/breweries.
Mud, Clay & Ceramics.player_build_guidance: Treat water as part of the production machine and the settlement identity. Cisterns, channels and kilns should be as visually important as houses.

Slime & Swamp Resources.why_here: Wetlands, herbal traditions and elevated settlement logic naturally accommodate slime basins, witch/potion support, mushrooms, reeds and other swamp renewables.
Slime & Swamp Resources.farm_architecture: Open slime basins below raised walkways, wash platforms, apothecary huts, mushroom sheds, reed drying racks, paper/weaving sheds and herb gardens.
Slime & Swamp Resources.settlement_expression: Dangerous/dirty production stays below or away from housing; lighter craft and market functions occupy boardwalk villages.
Slime & Swamp Resources.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Organic material can return toward compost systems; potion ingredients feed Hearthlands/other specialized brewing; slime supports Engineer's Reach mechanisms.
Slime & Swamp Resources.player_build_guidance: Let wetness drive the farm layout. Production should happen beneath, beside or between elevated inhabited platforms instead of forcing a dry-grid factory plan.

Lava, Basalt & Foundry.why_here: The caldera civilization formed around heat itself. Renewable lava, basalt work and heavy foundry processes are therefore civic infrastructure rather than foreign industry.
Lava, Basalt & Foundry.farm_architecture: Dripstone lava galleries, cauldron halls, heat channels, cooling courts, basalt works, forge arcades and heavy cargo quays.
Lava, Basalt & Foundry.settlement_expression: Lava harvesting, heavy forge craft, civic foundry and export harbor are separated by heat zones and connected by basalt causeways.
trade_routes: Ash Compact freight to Ember Coast
Lava, Basalt & Foundry.byproducts_and_secondary_uses: Heat infrastructure can support nearby processing but should not become an excuse to centralize unrelated industries here.
Lava, Basalt & Foundry.player_build_guidance: Show cooling, containment and worker safety architecturally. The farm should look dangerous but controlled.

phase_2_queue.goal: Extend the same integration depth to hostile, oceanic, transport, Nether and End ecosystems without losing completeness.
ecosystems: Fishing / Kelp / Drowned / Tidal Processing — Sunken Coast
Ocean & Guardian / Coral / Prismarine — Sapphire Coast
Nether Vegetation — Ember Coast while all wood-family output remains consolidated under Timberlands where required
End Obsidian & Special Systems — Shrouded Isles

cross_region_dependencies_started.flow: structural timber, specialty wood, repair stock, saplings
bulk stone, finished masonry, bridge craft
redstone components, automation modules, maintenance parts
sorting, buffering, contracts and redistribution rather than source processing
